clue.text: Solid, the rig, newly braced by engineer

indicators.note: to be braced is to be held firm on either side, so the engineer's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame

indicators.note: newly signals the words 'the rig' made over in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A rig judged sound because an engineer has fitted new braces to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' here means sound and leak-proof, not a state of matter; 'newly' rearranges the words before it, and 'braced by' puts that inside the engineer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Something watertight has no gaps or flaws, so an argument or seal described as solid fits.

clue.text: Chess player was hard to beat decisively

parts.note: one side in chess is White
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A chess opponent proved tough to defeat outright.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash is a sporting rout where the loser scores nothing, so as a verb it means to trounce.

clue.text: Club match

definitions.meaning: a club in sport is a side of players
to ... items is to pair them so they go together

explanation.definitionFit: A side is a group of players like a club, and teaming colours means pairing them so they go together.

clue.text: Rose pens elaborate reply

indicators.note: something elaborate is worked out intricately, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone called Rose writes a long, carefully composed answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer given back to someone is a reply.

clue.text: Network's omitted time for broadcast

indicators.note: omitted says a letter has been left out of the network word

parts.note: tissue is a fine woven network, and the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A TV network has dropped a time slot from its schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: TISSUE, a fine web or network, loses its T to leave the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it out publicly, as a broadcaster does.

clue.text: Fish house in which a party's held

indicators.note: held says one piece is kept inside another, here inside the house

parts.note: a hut is a small, simple house
Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A dwelling where a political party gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which ... held' is split around 'a party's'; LIB stands for Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat sea fish caught for food.

clue.text: Dead bird almost fed to policeman? Nonsense

indicators.note: fed to means placed inside, as food goes into a mouth, so these letters enter the policeman word

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
D is the abbreviation for dead, as on genealogies

indicators.note: almost means the bird word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: the swallow is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a policeman was fed a dead bird, and dismisses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to' means put inside, and 'almost' docks the bird's last letter; the question mark flags the policeman as an odd diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for rubbish talk or drivel.

clue.text: Title assigned to film about climbing

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A heading given to a film about mountaineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr is the form of address put before a man's name.

clue.text: South has to follow master cards

indicators.note: has to follow puts the south letter after the master word

parts.note: a master copy is the original

explanation.surface: At the bridge table, South must follow the leader's suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an eccentric person, and so is an oddball one-off.

clue.text: Deity with head of Egyptian fish

parts.note: Sol is the Roman sun god

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An Egyptian god depicted with a fish's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish such as the Dover variety.

clue.text: Dolly's a model

definitions.meaning: in cricket a dolly is an easy catch
an artist's model poses for a portrait

explanation.definitionFit: An easy catch in cricket and a person posing for a portrait share the same word.

clue.text: Floating freely above LEM

indicators.note: freely says the letters move about without fixed order

explanation.surface: A lunar module drifting free above the Moon's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges ABOVE LEM; LEM was the Apollo lunar module.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating as in a floating feast whose date is not fixed, able to shift.

clue.text: Final result of the Factory System, maybe

definitions.text: Final result of the Factory System, maybe

parts.words: Final result of the Factory System, maybe
parts.note: reads as what a manufacturing system turns out at the very end of its line, which is also any final outcome

explanation.definitionFit: The finished goods after all stages, and so any eventual outcome.

clue.text: Elevated, you'll see a Yorkshire river's winding length

indicators.note: a winding river twists, so the river's letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, flowing through Leeds

explanation.surface: From high up you can watch a Yorkshire river twist along its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges AIRE into ERIA; 'river's' reads as the river has.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerial means in the air or overhead, as in an aerial walkway.

clue.text: Given a hand, a second of the same kind-short on diamonds

indicators.note: on places the diamonds letter after what goes before in an across entry
short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: a sister ship or company is one of the same kind
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone helped with a near-identical item that lacks diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assisted is to be helped, which is what lending a hand does.

clue.text: Vagrant roaming America's a slow one

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: US is short for America

explanation.surface: A tramp wandering America is a dull character.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, slow in the sense of dim.

clue.text: Cited changes around theatre in bad shape

indicators.note: around places the first piece on both sides of the theatre word
changes says the letters of the word are altered in order

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: Quoted alterations to a run-down theatre building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' gives DECIT and 'around' puts it about the theatre word; rep is short for repertory.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out by age or neglect.

clue.text: Mirth subsequently overcoming disgusted expression

indicators.note: overcoming is read as coming over, so the first word surrounds the other

parts.note: later means subsequently
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Amusement later wins over a look of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound of mirth or merriment.

clue.text: Climber in High Street, painting

parts.note: up means high
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A mountaineer in the main street of a town, painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber who has risen fast and acts above their station.

clue.text: Line by river should identify him

definitions.text: Line by river should identify him

parts.note: to angle is to fish with hook and line

explanation.surface: A fishing line on the riverbank shows who is there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a fisherman, whose line beside the river gives him away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fishes with rod and line from a riverbank.

clue.text: Departed packing a new woolly

indicators.note: packing means holding something inside, as a case holds clothes

parts.note: late means departed, dead

explanation.surface: Someone who has left packed a new woolly jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanate is a botanical term for covered in woolly hairs.

clue.text: Permit for dance entertainment

parts.note: pas is a ballet step
sport means fun or entertainment

explanation.surface: Is a licence needed for dance shows?
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document that permits crossing borders.

clue.text: Club finished East

parts.note: past means over, finished

explanation.surface: A club in the east has closed.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste someone is to beat or thrash them, as with a club.

clue.text: Cut back dead fruit first

indicators.note: first puts the fruit word ahead of the dead letter

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum

explanation.surface: Trim the dead growth before picking fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pruned means trimmed or cut down, like a shrub.

clue.text: Check old block

parts.note: to vet is to check carefully

explanation.surface: Inspect an ancient obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the power to block or forbid a measure.

clue.text: Instrument, one carried by British vessel

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the following letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a means one

explanation.surface: A musical instrument taken aboard a British ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A double bass or bass guitar is a low-pitched musical instrument.

clue.text: Showing signs of inflation?

parts.note: reads as a comment on rising prices, but means filled with air, like a tyre

explanation.definitionFit: Pneumatic describes things worked by or filled with compressed air, so swollen.

clue.text: About to appear in nattiest new suit

indicators.note: to appear in means set within the following letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the word's letters

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on a subject

explanation.surface: Getting ready to show up in the smartest new suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives ATTENTIS; 'suit' is courtship, not clothing, as in paying suit to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying suit to someone means courting them, offering romantic attentions.
